fields.name: sess
fields.assembly_method: server-baked into cap_union_prehandle JSONP, carried in iframe URL ?sess=, then rotated by /cap_union_new_getsig responses via updateSession()
fields.provenance: Module 30 caches sess in a module-private `a.sess` slot, seeds it from window.captchaConfig.sess, exposes queryMap() that copies it into `d`, and exposes updateSession() which module 56 calls from the getsig + verify success handlers (`e.sess && w(e.sess)`) to rotate the value mid-session.

fields.name: cdata
fields.assembly_method: module 56 IIFE (`function(e,t,n){...e.cdata=n}(d,n)`) using l.challenge() from module 72
fields.provenance: Module 72 (n(73) = md5) brute-forces a PoW challenge (t.randstr||n for n < t.M) when window.captchaConfig.capChallenge is populated, returns the counter as a number; module 56 stores that number in `d.cdata`.

fields.name: ans
fields.assembly_method: module 56 (`d.ans=c`) after concatenating slide-drag coord string c
fields.provenance: Built by iterating the per-step coordinate array produced by the slide drag handler (module 67) and concatenating `Math.floor(left)+","+Math.floor(top)+";"` for each point. In the HAR this reduces to a single "484,46;" — one coarse-grained drop point.

fields.name: vsig
fields.assembly_method: module 56 (`d.vsig=_.vsig`) reading window.captchaConfig.vsig
fields.provenance: vsig is a server-provided per-challenge token carried in captchaConfig and refreshed by /cap_union_new_getsig responses (`t&&(_.vsig=t)`). In this HAR it is empty.

fields.name: websig
fields.assembly_method: module 56 (`d.websig=_.websig`) reading window.captchaConfig.websig
fields.provenance: Server-baked in the show-page captchaConfig block; empty in this HAR.

fields.name: subcapclass
fields.assembly_method: module 56 (`d.subcapclass=_.subcapclass`) reading window.captchaConfig.subcapclass
fields.provenance: Server-baked in the show-page captchaConfig block; empty in this HAR.

fields.name: pow_answer
fields.assembly_method: module 56 (`d.pow_answer=...`) set from the WebWorker PoW result object M.ans
fields.provenance: When window.captchaConfig.powCfg.md5 and .prefix are present, module 56 runs a WebWorker (module 48 -> worker in module 49 -> hash in module 52) to brute-force an md5 prefix, then sets `d.pow_answer = P.nonce + M.ans`. Empty in this HAR because powCfg is absent.

fields.name: pow_calc_time
fields.assembly_method: module 56 (`d.pow_calc_time=M.duration`)
fields.provenance: Duration (ms) of the PoW WebWorker run, captured alongside the result. Zero in this HAR.

fields.name: collect
fields.assembly_method: module 56 (`e[_.collectdata]=decodeURIComponent(C())`) using tdc.getData() from module 38/70
fields.provenance: Module 38 wraps `window.TDC.getData(true)` (tdc.js register-VM output); module 70 re-exports it as `tdc.getData`; module 56 reads it through `C = E.getData` and URL-decodes into the field whose name is whatever the server chose for `_.collectdata` (here "collect"). This is the same `collect` token produced by the register-VM tdc.js described in docs/TOKEN_FORMAT.md.

fields.name: tlg
fields.assembly_method: module 56 (`e.tlg=e[_.collectdata].length`)
fields.provenance: Length in characters of the URL-decoded collect-token string — cheap client-side integrity tag.

fields.name: fpinfo
fields.assembly_method: module 56 (`d.fpinfo=i`) from the vm.run callback `o => i` chain; `i` is the outer `fpinfo` wrapped in the run callback
fields.provenance: In the vm.run completion handler module 56 receives per-drag fingerprint data as `i` and stores it on `d.fpinfo`. Empty in this HAR because vm is not armed (vmAvailable empty, vmByteCode empty).

fields.name: eks
fields.assembly_method: module 56 (`d.eks=R()`) calling tdc.getEks() from module 38/70
fields.provenance: Module 38 exposes `getEks: function(){ return (window.TDC.getInfo()||{}).info || ""; }`; module 70 re-exports as `tdc.getEks`; module 56 reads via `R = E.getEks`. This is exactly the `eks` string server-baked into tdc.js line 123 and surfaced through `TDC.getInfo().info`, consistent with docs/EKS_FORMAT.md.

fields.name: nonce
fields.assembly_method: module 56 (`_.nonce && (d.nonce=_.nonce)`)
fields.provenance: Module 56 reads `window.captchaConfig.nonce`, which is server-baked into the show-page HTML alongside sess (confirmed in the HAR show-page body: `nonce:"eda1152f11f1daf0"`). The orchestrator never mutates it; it is passed through from the captchaConfig block into the verify body.

fields.name: vlg
fields.assembly_method: module 71 (`t.vlg=[vmAvailable?1:0, vmByteCode?1:0, 1].join("_")`), merged into `d` via `$.extend(d, o)` in module 56
fields.provenance: vlg is a three-digit availability signal for the stack-VM integration: "vmAvailable flag _ vmByteCode-nonempty flag _ 1". In this HAR both flags are 0 because captchaConfig.vmAvailable and captchaConfig.vmByteCode are empty strings.

fields.name: vData
fields.assembly_method: ORIGIN UNRESOLVED STATICALLY (see FLOW.md §9)
fields.provenance: The only textual `vData` write in the orchestrator bundle is inside the isLowIE() branch: `o=window.getVData && window.getVData(n.join("&")); o && (e.vData=o)`. `getVData` is not defined in t_captcha_slide.js (this bundle), tdc.js (grep: 0 hits), or vm_slide.js (grep: 0 hits — but vm_slide.js is the stack-VM encoded blob, so runtime behavior is opaque). On the HAR (Chrome 146, isLowIE false) vData is nevertheless present in the POST body. The static trace ends here; either vm-slide.enc.js installs window.getVData at runtime, or it installs a $.ajaxSettings data-filter / jQuery 1.11.3 prefilter that rewrites POST bodies before they hit the network.
